tests.notes: an internal function with a storage array parameter writes through to the caller's state variable; no copy is made
a storage struct parameter is a reference; field writes modify the original struct in place
storage reference parameters are allowed on private functions as well as internal ones
a fixed-size storage array can be passed as a storage parameter
passing the same state array as two storage parameters makes them alias the same storage; compile-level check only, the runtime aliasing result is not verified here
a storage parameter can be forwarded to another internal function; the reference is passed along, not copied
a single element of a storage array of structs can be passed as a storage reference
delete on an element reached through a storage parameter resets that element; deleting the reference itself is disallowed (see storage/010)
a helper with a storage array parameter can read and write several elements of the caller's state array
public functions cannot take storage parameters; a raw storage reference has no ABI representation
external functions cannot take storage parameters; same root cause as 010
reference-type parameters must state their data location explicitly, even on internal functions
a memory array cannot be passed where a storage reference parameter is expected; parameter-passing counterpart of location_conversions/010
